hook: For just £25, Arthur Conan Doyle agreed to relinquish all rights to A Study in Scarlet.

sections.voiceover: For just £25, Arthur Conan Doyle agreed to relinquish all rights to A Study in Scarlet.
sections.visual_cue: Close shot of an antique brass balance scale resting on weathered manuscript paper.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft paper rustle followed by a quiet metal coin clink.
b_roll: 19th century fountain pen writing on parchment

sections.voiceover: In December 1887, Beeton's Christmas Annual published the first Sherlock Holmes tale. Where would that £25 release head?
sections.visual_cue: Archival engraving of Victorian London streets in winter alongside the cover of Beeton's Christmas Annual.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle Victorian street sounds and soft low woodwind tone.
b_roll: Beeton's Christmas Annual 1887 title page illustration
Victorian London gas lamps and horse carriage movement

sections.voiceover: Except that magazine release in Beeton's Christmas Annual was just the start.
sections.visual_cue: Camera zooms out from printing press machinery onto a stack of bound book pages.

sections.voiceover: Ward, Lock & Co. published the First British Book Edition in 1888. J.B. Lippincott Company published the First American Book Edition in 1890. That launch expanded to sixty tales featuring Sherlock Holmes.
sections.visual_cue: Split frame showing early book editions from Ward, Lock & Co. and J.B. Lippincott Company with historical publication dates.
sections.sfx_cue: Turning book pages sound and rising string swell.
b_roll: 1888 British edition title page archive image

sections.voiceover: For £25, Arthur Conan Doyle relinquished all story rights.
